title: Fill PDF Form Online – Fill In PDF Forms Free, No Upload
description: Fill in a PDF form in your browser: type in text fields, tick boxes, pick options, and flatten the answers on save if you want. Free, nothing uploaded.
heading: Fill a PDF form
subtitle: Type into a PDF form's fields, tick its boxes and save a filled copy; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Fill in a PDF form online: type into its text fields, tick checkboxes, choose radio buttons and drop-down options, then save a filled copy. Tick Flatten on save to make the answers part of the page so they cannot be changed. Arabic answers work, and the form is filled in your browser, so it is never uploaded.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your file is handled by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees it.

features.title: Every common field
features.text: Text fields, checkboxes, radio buttons and drop-down lists, in English or Arabic.

features.title: Flatten on save
features.text: Make the answers part of the page, so the copy you send can't be changed.

stepsTitle: How to fill in a PDF form

steps.title: Choose your PDF form
steps.text: Click Choose a file, or drop a PDF on the page.

steps.title: Fill it in
steps.text: Click each field and type, tick or choose your answer.

steps.title: Save a copy
steps.text: Tick Flatten on save if the answers should be fixed, then click Save a copy and download the filled form.

handles: Fields: text fields, multi-line boxes, checkboxes, radio buttons and drop-down lists.
Languages: answers in English, Arabic or any language your keyboard types.
Flatten on save: answers drawn onto the page and the fields removed.
Forms without fields: detected, with a pointer to Edit PDF for adding text boxes.
limits: Only PDFs with real form fields can be filled; for a scanned or plain form, use Edit PDF to add text boxes.
XFA forms (made with Adobe LiveCycle) are not supported.
Flattened answers are drawn as pictures, so they can't be selected or searched.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your file is read and changed by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload.

faq.question: What does Flatten on save do?
faq.answer: It draws every answer onto the page and removes the form fields, so the copy can't be changed in other PDF apps. Leave it off to keep the fields fillable.

faq.question: Why can't I click anything in my form?
faq.answer: The PDF probably has no form fields: it is a scan or a plain page that looks like a form. Use Edit PDF to place text boxes on it instead.

faq.question: Is my original file changed?
faq.answer: No. Save a copy makes a new PDF to download; the file on your device stays exactly as it was.

faq.question: Can I use a password-protected PDF?
faq.answer: Not directly: a PDF that needs a password to open can't be read by this tool. If you know the password, remove it with Unlock PDF, which also runs in your browser, then try again.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark of ours and no limit on how often you use it.

faq.question: How do I fill out a PDF form without Adobe Acrobat?
faq.answer: A PDF form with fillable fields can be filled in any browser: open it in OpenAnyDoc's Fill PDF form tool, click each field, type your answers and save a copy. Nothing is uploaded, and Flatten on save fixes the answers so they can't be changed. To only read a PDF, see how to open a PDF without Adobe.
